    AI safety

    SafeGPT — cloud behavioral intelligence

    Most cameras detect events. SafeGPT understands behavior. The difference is whether the fatigued driver gets pulled over before the crash, or whether the crash gets recorded for the insurance claim.

    The problem SafeGPT solves

    A 200-truck fleet running traditional cameras generates 500–1,000 alerts per day. Most are false positives — a pothole, a mirror glance, a shadow.

    The safety manager reviews everything on Monday, skims on Wednesday, ignores by Friday. The fleet paid for cameras but didn't get safety. SafeGPT changes the architecture.

    Instead of firing an alert for every individual event on-device, the camera streams rich behavioral metadata every second — speed, G-sensor, lane position, following distance, gaze direction, blink rate, vehicle CAN data — to the cloud. SafeGPT analyses all these streams together, identifying behavioral patterns no single sensor can detect alone.

    Six core SafeGPT capabilities

    CapabilityHow it worksWhat your fleet gets
    90% event reductionOnly alerts when combined behavioral patterns indicate genuine risk — not individual sensor triggers10–20 critical events/day, not 500 noise alerts. Reviews take 20 min, not 3 hours.
    Early fatigue detectionCorrelates lane-position degradation + speed oscillation + blink-rate changes + steering input varianceDetects fatigue 5–15 minutes before the driver's eyes close. Intervention while still safe.
    Risk type classificationTags every event by category: fatigue, distraction, aggressive driving, potential impairment, environmental hazardRight events to the right stakeholders. Monitoring centres only get events matching their mandate.
    Multi-sensor accident detectionConfirms collisions by correlating G-sensor + speed change + lane departure + driver reaction + CAN dataEliminates pothole false positives. Catches low-speed parking collisions G-sensor alone misses.
    Behavioral taggingBuilds persistent driver profiles with specific tags: chronic tailgater, night-fatigue prone, excellent cornering, smooth brakingTargeted coaching on specific patterns. Positive tags enable gamification and recognition.
    Coaching prioritisationAuto-ranks video clips by coaching impact based on each driver's behavioral profileSafety manager finds the right clip for the right driver instantly. No more searching footage.

    Evidence Cards — solving the AI black-box problem

    The most common objection to AI safety systems: "the system says this is an event, but the fleet manager doesn't understand why."

    Evidence Cards show the visual explanation for every event — which signals contributed, how they deviated from the driver's baseline, and what pattern triggered the alert.

    Coaching conversations shift from "the camera says you did something wrong" to "here's what the data shows — your lane position was degrading and your blink rate had changed, indicating early-stage fatigue. Let's talk about your sleep schedule."

    How to read the detections below

    Each AI detection has a short explanation, a sample clip (placeholder for now), and a parameter guide — what each setting controls and which way to adjust it. Tap a detection to expand it. Three settings recur across most features:

    • Sensitivity — how readily the feature fires. Higher = earlier/more alerts but more false positives.
    • Minimum speed / speed gating — the speed band a feature is active in, so it doesn't alert when parked or crawling.
    • Duration / threshold — how long or how far the behaviour must persist before it counts (e.g. seconds of gaze-off-road).

    ADAS — forward-facing detections

    Forward Collision Warning (FCW)ADAS

    Warns when you're closing on the vehicle ahead too fast for the gap — a likely rear-end. The forward camera estimates time-to-collision and alerts the driver to brake.

    Sample clip
    Forward Collision Warning (FCW) — sample clipComing soon
    Configure parameters
    ParameterWhat it controlsHow to adjust
    Sensitivity (Low / Med / High)How early the warning fires (a longer time-to-collision trips it sooner).Raise for cautious fleets; lower to cut nuisance alerts in dense, slow traffic.
    Minimum activation speedFCW only runs above this speed.Raise it to silence stop-and-go false alarms in city driving.
    Alert modalityAudio, on-screen, and/or seat vibration.Use audio+visual as default; reserve vibration for critical fleets.

    Set these in CMS → AI Settings. Exact default values and ranges vary by camera model — check the device config; this guide explains what each parameter means.

    DMS — driver-facing detections

    Fatigue / DrowsinessDMS

    Detects eye closure, microsleep and prolonged blinks. Streamax runs two-layer fatigue AI — rule-based plus a deep-learning model trained on millions of real fatigue events — to catch edge cases (small eyes, long lashes). With the C29N DMS at A-pillar eye level (940 nm IR) it works at night and through sunglasses. SafeGPT can flag fatigue 5–15 minutes before the eyes close.

    Sample clip
    Fatigue / Drowsiness — sample clipComing soon
    Configure parameters
    ParameterWhat it controlsHow to adjust
    SensitivityEye-closure duration / blink pattern that triggers an alert.Raise for night / long-haul shifts where fatigue risk is highest.
    Minimum speedOnly evaluates while the vehicle is moving.Keeps it from alerting when parked.
    Alert modalityAudio, visual, and seat vibration.Enable seat vibration for critical drowsiness events.

    Set these in CMS → AI Settings. Exact default values and ranges vary by camera model — check the device config; this guide explains what each parameter means.

    Recommended starting profiles by fleet type

    Start here, then re-tune after week 2 once you've seen your baseline event rate. Your CSM can review the data with you on a 30-min call.

    Fleet typeRecommended starting profileWhy
    Long-haul truckingStandard ADAS + High DMSFatigue is the #1 risk; following-distance varies with traffic.
    Urban deliveryHigh ADAS + Standard DMSFrequent pedestrians, cyclists, sudden stops.
    Transit busStandard ADAS + High DMSPublic-safety scrutiny is highest in this segment.
    Mining / haul truckCustom mining profileStandard ADAS triggers constantly off-road; mining profile filters dust/glare.
    Taxi / rideshareStandard ADAS + High distractionPhone use is the dominant risk.

    Five-layer sensor fusion — where this is heading

    SafeGPT today fuses video + driver-state + behavioral data. By H1 2027, every Streamax camera will integrate five intelligence layers in one device:

    LayerIntelligenceProvides
    L1: EyesVideo AI (ADAS + DMS)FCW, LDW, pedestrian detection, fatigue, phone use, seatbelt
    L2: FeelAdvanced maneuver recognition150+ risky-driving types — cornering, lane handling, braking — calibrated across billions of miles
    L3: KnowNative vehicle CAN/J1939/OBD-IIRPM, fuel, brake application, transmission, fault codes
    L4: LocateGPS positioning & trip recordingReal-time location, route deviation, geofencing
    L5: ThinkSafeGPT cloud behavioral fusionContinuous analysis of L1–L4. Predicts risk before events occur.
